canonical_name: Hall's marriage theorem (exact one-side versus perfect-matching scope open)
source_attribution: Philip Hall, 1935 (catalog metadata and bibliographic identity)
literal_source_claim_zh: 二部图完美匹配存在的条件
literal_source_claim_en: A condition for the existence of a perfect matching in a bipartite graph.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not define perfect matching, bipartition coverage, neighborhood, finiteness, balance, quantifier scope, or theorem direction. The standard Hall graph theorem gives a matching saturating one bipartition, while mathlib's IsPerfectMatching saturates every graph vertex and its direct sufficient theorem uses a global subset condition. Choosing either without a source decision would substitute or broaden the received claim.
domain_and_universes: Open: finite indexed families; the source's finite-relation specialization or pinned relations with finite singleton fibers / finite codomain; or a simple graph G on a universe-polymorphic vertex type V. Finite versus arbitrary index scope, local finiteness, selected bipartition sets, coverage, disjointness, and balance assumptions all remain statement-phase decisions.
conclusion: Open as an exact expression: either distinct representatives, a matching saturating one chosen bipartition, or a graph-wide perfect matching under source-approved assumptions.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake. Empty index types and parts, empty/edgeless graphs, isolated vertices, empty candidate sets, singleton parts, unequal part sizes, uncovered vertices, and infinite locally finite graphs remain explicit statement decisions.
